faqs.question: How do I join ASME?
faqs.answer: Fill out the interest form on our Join page. A team lead will follow up with next steps. Freshmen through seniors are welcome, no prior experience required.

faqs.question: Is there a membership fee?
faqs.answer: There's a small national ASME dues fee (~$30/year) that covers your professional membership and access to ASME resources. The Iowa chapter itself is free to join. Scholarships are available if cost is an issue.

faqs.question: Do I need engineering experience?
faqs.answer: Nope. Most members are mechanical engineering students but we welcome anyone interested in hands-on building — electrical, aerospace, industrial, CS, even non-engineers. You'll learn by doing.

faqs.question: Where is ASME located on campus?
faqs.answer: Our workspace is in the Seamans Center for Engineering on the University of Iowa campus. Most meetings happen in engineering classrooms nearby. Check the calendar for specific rooms.

faqs.question: What competition teams do you have?
faqs.answer: We have three main competition teams: IAM3D (lunar rover + 3D-printed chassis), Student Design Competition (yearly engineering challenge), and MATE ROV (underwater remotely operated vehicle).

faqs.question: What is IAM3D?
faqs.answer: IAM3D (Innovative Additive Manufacturing 3D) is the ASME national additive manufacturing competition. Our team is designing the Crater Cruncher — a lunar rover with a 6-DOF robotic arm, custom drivetrain, and 3D-printed chassis.

faqs.question: What is MATE ROV?
faqs.answer: MATE ROV stands for Marine Advanced Technology Education Remotely Operated Vehicle. Our team designs an underwater ROV — propulsion, control systems, manipulators, and cameras — to complete timed mission tasks in a pool.

faqs.question: Can I start my own project?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. If you have an idea that fits the ASME mission, pitch it to the exec team. We can help with funding, space, tools, and recruiting teammates.

faqs.question: How do I submit a 3D print request?
faqs.answer: Log in to the member portal → click Prints → fill out the form with your filament, file (.3mf), and notes. An admin will approve it and queue it on the H2S or P1S printer.

faqs.question: What printers do you have?
faqs.answer: We have two Bambu Lab printers: the H2S (larger, faster, supports multi-material) and the P1S (enclosed, great for ABS and PETG). Both accept sliced .3mf files from BambuStudio.

faqs.question: Is printing free for members?
faqs.answer: Printing is free for small member projects and coursework. Large multi-hour jobs or competition parts may be prioritized by team need. Bring your own filament for custom colors if we don't stock them.

faqs.question: What file format do I need?
faqs.answer: Upload a sliced .3mf file from BambuStudio. This includes your slicing settings and picks the right profile for our machines. Raw STL files aren't accepted — slice them in BambuStudio first.

faqs.question: When are general meetings?
faqs.answer: General body meetings are typically bi-weekly during the semester. Exact times vary — check the calendar on our Events page or in the member portal.

faqs.question: How do I RSVP to an event?
faqs.answer: Log in to the member portal → Calendar → click RSVP next to the event. You can also check in at the door with your NFC tag.

faqs.question: Do you have social events?
faqs.answer: Yes — cookouts, intramural sports, game nights, and end-of-semester socials. Building engineering skills matters, but so does the community. Follow our Instagram for announcements.

faqs.question: How do I contact a team lead?
faqs.answer: Use the Contact page to send a message. Team-specific questions can go to the team lead listed on each project page.

faqs.question: Where can I find you on social media?
How do I become a sponsor?
faqs.answer: We love working with industry partners. Sponsor funds go directly to materials, tools, travel, and competition costs. Visit the Sponsors page for partnership tiers and an inquiry form.
